# Cantrip.Descriptions

Rules text: what a card says, worked out from what it does, through a phrase table a game can translate.

Part of [the API reference](README.md). The guides are [docs/csharp.md](../csharp.md) and [docs/godot.md](../godot.md); when something here surprises you, [docs/troubleshooting.md](../troubleshooting.md) is the other end of it.

| Type | |
|---|---|
| [`Description`](#description) | The rules text of one entity: segments of plain text and linked values, the flavour line kept apart, and tooltips for every keyword the text relies on. |
| [`DescriptionBuilder`](#descriptionbuilder) | Builds descriptions for every kind of entity. One walk over a definition's effects both generates the automatic text and names every value in it (`damage`, `damage2`, `block`, `Poison`...), which is what links a writer's `{placeholders}` to the real effect. |
| [`DescriptionLevel`](#descriptionlevel) | Which of the three description levels (automatic, custom, override) produced the text. |
| [`DescriptionSegment`](#descriptionsegment) | One run of a description. Values are kept apart from the words around them so a UI can colour buffed numbers, show a breakdown on hover, or strike through the printed value. |
| [`EnglishDescriptions`](#englishdescriptions) | The built-in English phrases. Subclass it to change a few phrases, or implement `IDescriptionLocalizer` directly for a full translation. |
| [`IDescriptionLocalizer`](#idescriptionlocalizer) | Supplies descriptions in another language. The library owns the templates and placeholders; a game owns the translations. Return null from any member to fall back to the content's own text or the built-in English phrase. |

## Description

```csharp
public sealed class Description
```

The rules text of one entity: segments of plain text and linked values, the flavour line kept apart, and tooltips for every keyword the text relies on.

### Properties

```csharp
public string? Against { get; }
```

Who this is aimed at, by name, for a description that has a target of its own: the member an enemy is telegraphing against. Null for everything else, including an intent that has not been rolled.

It is a name rather than an entity because a description is data a UI keeps across a frame, and an entity is not. A game that wants the id asks the runtime.

```csharp
public DescriptionSegment? Cost { get; }
```

The card's cost as a live value, for the corner of the card frame, or null when the entity has no cost. It is not part of `Description.Segments`.

```csharp
public EntityDefinition? Definition { get; }
```

What this describes, or null for a description built from something other than a definition, such as an enemy's rolled intent.

```csharp
public string? Flavour { get; }
```

The flavour line. Never mixed into the rules text.

```csharp
public bool IsEmpty { get; }
```

Whether there is anything to show. True for a definition with no effect, no listeners and no modifiers (a vanilla card), so a UI can leave the rules box out rather than draw an empty one.

```csharp
public DescriptionLevel Level { get; }
```

Which of the three levels produced this text. Worth checking before offering a designer's tooling: at `DescriptionLevel.Override` the values are not live, so nothing in `Description.Values` will change however the game goes.

```csharp
public string Name { get; }
```

Display name, localized when the localizer supplies one.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<DescriptionSegment> Segments { get; }
```

The text in order, split so that values can be drawn differently from the words around them. Concatenating their `DescriptionSegment.Text` is `Description.ToPlainText`.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<KeywordTooltip> Tooltips { get; }
```

One entry for every keyword or status the text relies on, flattened: a keyword that mentions another appears once here rather than nested, so a UI can show them as a flat list without walking a tree or guarding against a cycle.

```csharp
public IEnumerable<DescriptionSegment> Values { get; }
```

Just the values, in order: the numbers a tooltip or a comparison view wants without the prose. Evaluated on each enumeration.

### Methods

```csharp
public DescriptionSegment? Find(string placeholder)
```

The first value in the text linked to `placeholder`, if any.

```csharp
public string ToLine()
```

The whole thing on one line, as an intent panel shows it: "Cutthroat → Vestal: Deal 8 damage and apply 2 Bleeding." The name and the target are left out when there are none, so a description with neither is just its text.

```csharp
public string ToMarkup()
```

The text with changed values shown against their printed value, as in "~~6~~ 9". Unchanged values print once.

```csharp
public string ToPlainText()
```

The text with current values, for logs, tests and plain labels.

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

The same as `Description.ToPlainText`: the current values, no markup, no name and no target.

## DescriptionBuilder

```csharp
public sealed class DescriptionBuilder
```

Builds descriptions for every kind of entity. One walk over a definition's effects both generates the automatic text and names every value in it (`damage`, `damage2`, `block`, `Poison`...), which is what links a writer's `{placeholders}` to the real effect.

### Constructors

```csharp
public DescriptionBuilder(ContentLibrary content, IDescriptionLocalizer? localizer = null)
```

A builder over a loaded library. It is reusable and holds no per-description state, so a game makes one and keeps it.

**Parameters.**

- `content`: The library whose definitions will be described.
- `localizer`: Where names, rules text and phrases come from. Null uses `EnglishDescriptions.Instance`. The localizer is consulted on every build, so switching language means making a new builder rather than rebuilding the content.

### Fields and constants

```csharp
public const string IgnoredText = "CT403"
```

Note: a `text:` that is never shown, because the same definition also sets `text_override:`.

```csharp
public const string StaleText = "CT402"
```

Warning: the effect has changed since the `text_checked` hash was recorded, so the hand-written text may now describe something the card no longer does.

```csharp
public const string UnknownPlaceholder = "CT401"
```

Warning: a `{placeholder}` in a writer's `text:` that matches nothing in the effect, so it is shown as written.

### Methods

```csharp
public Description Describe(Entity entity, CardRuntime runtime, Entity? target = null)
```

Describes a live entity. Values go through the modifier pipeline exactly as the rules would use them now: damage through `damage` (and `damage_taken` when a target is given), costs as `CardRuntime.CostOf(Entity)` computes them, stacks as they stand.

```csharp
public Description Describe(EntityDefinition definition)
```

Describes a definition with its printed values, as in a card library or wiki.

```csharp
public Description DescribeIntent(Entity enemy, CardRuntime runtime)
```

Describes what an enemy intends to do on its next turn, and who to: "Cutthroat → Vestal: Deal 8 damage and apply 2 Bleeding" as `Description.ToLine` prints it. Empty while intents have not been rolled, which is also what a UI should show then.

```csharp
public Description DescribeMove(EntityDefinition definition, string moveName, CardRuntime? runtime = null, Entity? enemy = null, Entity? against = null)
```

Describes a single enemy move, which is what an intent panel shows: "Deal 11 damage to you", not the enemy's whole repertoire. Pass the runtime and the enemy as well to get the numbers it would actually deal now, modifiers and all.

**Parameters.**

- `definition`: The enemy's definition, which is where the move is written.
- `moveName`: The move to describe, by the name its header gives it.
- `runtime`: The live game, for the numbers the move would deal now.
- `enemy`: The enemy making it, whose own modifiers are part of those numbers.
- `against`: Who the move is aimed at, for the numbers and for the line it prints. Null reads the leader, which is what it meant when a side had one member.

```csharp
public static string EffectHash(EntityDefinition definition)
```

A stable fingerprint of everything that affects the rules of a definition, and nothing that only affects presentation. Record it as `text_checked "<hash>"`.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Validate(EntityDefinition definition)
```

Drift protection: CT401 for placeholders that point at nothing, CT402 when the effect has changed since the writer recorded `text_checked`, CT403 when `text` is shadowed.

## DescriptionLevel

```csharp
public enum DescriptionLevel
```

Which of the three description levels (automatic, custom, override) produced the text.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Auto = 0` | Generated from the effect tree, listeners and modifiers. Nothing to write. |
| `Custom = 1` | The writer's `text:`, with `{placeholders}` still linked to the effect. |
| `Override = 2` | `text_override:`, shown verbatim with no live values. |

## DescriptionSegment

```csharp
public sealed class DescriptionSegment
```

One run of a description. Values are kept apart from the words around them so a UI can colour buffed numbers, show a breakdown on hover, or strike through the printed value.

### Properties

```csharp
public Num Base { get; }
```

The value before the modifier pipeline: the printed number.

```csharp
public string BaseText { get; }
```

The printed value, for "~~6~~ 9" style displays.

```csharp
public Num Current { get; }
```

The value after every active modifier, exactly as the rules would use it now.

```csharp
public bool HasNumber { get; }
```

False for symbolic values such as `X`, which carry only their `DescriptionSegment.Text`.

```csharp
public bool IsChanged { get; }
```

Whether a modifier has moved this number away from the printed one, which is what `Description.ToMarkup` strikes through. Always false for a symbolic value, which has no number to compare.

```csharp
public bool IsLinked { get; }
```

Whether this value is tied to a named part of the effect, and can therefore be looked up with `Description.Find(string)`. Automatic text links everything it generates; a writer's `text:` links whatever its `{placeholders}` name.

```csharp
public SegmentKind Kind { get; }
```

Whether this run is words or a value. Note that a value is not always a number: see `DescriptionSegment.HasNumber`, which is false for symbolic ones such as `X`.

```csharp
public bool LowerIsBetter { get; }
```

True for costs, where a smaller number is the good direction.

```csharp
public string? Placeholder { get; }
```

The placeholder this value is linked to (`damage`, `Poison`...), if any.

```csharp
public string Text { get; }
```

What is shown: the words, or the current value formatted for display.

```csharp
public ValueTrend Trend { get; }
```

Which way the change went for whoever holds the entity, with costs already accounted for: a cost that went down is `ValueTrend.Buffed`, not decreased. Colour from this rather than from comparing `DescriptionSegment.Current` with `DescriptionSegment.Base`, which gets a cost backwards.

```csharp
public string? Unit { get; }
```

The unit written in content, such as `%`. Only `%` is shown.

### Methods

```csharp
public static DescriptionSegment Number(Num baseValue, Num current, string? placeholder = null, string? unit = null, bool lowerIsBetter = false)
```

A computed value. `baseValue` is what it is before any modifier applies.

```csharp
public static DescriptionSegment Plain(string text)
```

A run of fixed words. Games build these when they assemble text of their own around a description; everything inside a description is built by the description builder.

```csharp
public static DescriptionSegment Symbol(string text, string? placeholder = null)
```

A value that cannot be known until the effect runs, such as the stacks of a status that is described on its own or the energy spent on an X-cost card. Shown as its phrase.

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

What is shown, which for a value is the current number and not the printed one.

## EnglishDescriptions

```csharp
public class EnglishDescriptions : IDescriptionLocalizer
```

The built-in English phrases. Subclass it to change a few phrases, or implement `IDescriptionLocalizer` directly for a full translation.

### Fields and constants

```csharp
public static readonly EnglishDescriptions Instance
```

The shared instance, which a builder given no localizer uses. It holds no state, so one is enough; a subclass that overrides a few phrases makes its own.

### Properties

```csharp
public static IEnumerable<string> Keys { get; }
```

Every phrase key, for translators.

### Methods

```csharp
public virtual string? Flavour(EntityDefinition definition)
```

Null, so the definition's own flavour line is used.

```csharp
public virtual string? Name(EntityDefinition definition)
```

Null, so the definition's own name is used. Override it to rename things without touching content.

```csharp
public virtual string? Phrase(string key)
```

The built-in English phrase for a key, or null for a key that has none. This is the one member that does not default to null, which is why subclassing this class rather than implementing the interface gives a translation that still reads correctly where it is incomplete.

```csharp
public virtual string? Text(EntityDefinition definition)
```

Null, so the definition's own `text:` or generated text is used.

## IDescriptionLocalizer

```csharp
public interface IDescriptionLocalizer
```

Supplies descriptions in another language. The library owns the templates and placeholders; a game owns the translations. Return null from any member to fall back to the content's own text or the built-in English phrase.

Every member defaults to null, which is "I have no translation for this", so a localizer implements only the parts it has, and a member added in a later release does not break one written today. See [Stability](https://github.com/AGomnes/Cantrip/blob/main/docs/stability.md).

### Methods

```csharp
virtual string? Flavour(EntityDefinition definition)
```

The flavour line in this language. It is kept apart from the rules text and never mixed into it, so a translation can drop it entirely by returning an empty string.

```csharp
virtual string? Name(EntityDefinition definition)
```

The display name of a definition.

```csharp
virtual string? Phrase(string key)
```

A phrase template used by generated text, such as `deal` = `"Deal {amount} {type}damage{target}{ignore}."`. See `EnglishDescriptions.Keys`.

The default answers null, which falls back to the built-in English phrase, so a localizer that translates only names and rules text still reads correctly.

```csharp
virtual string? Text(EntityDefinition definition)
```

The definition's rules text in this language, using the same `{placeholders}` as its `text:`. When the definition uses `text_override:`, this replaces that instead.

## KeywordTooltip

```csharp
public sealed class KeywordTooltip
```

A generated explanation of a status or keyword the described entity refers to.

### Properties

```csharp
public EntityDefinition Definition { get; }
```

The keyword or status this explains, so a UI can key an icon or a lookup off it.

```csharp
public Description Description { get; }
```

The keyword's own description. Its `Description.Tooltips` is empty: keywords it mentions in turn are flattened into the top-level tooltip list instead, so a UI shows each keyword once however deeply they reference each other.

```csharp
public string Name { get; }
```

The keyword's display name, localized. This is what the text being explained says.

### Methods

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

The tooltip on one line, for a log or a test. A UI wants `KeywordTooltip.Description`, which keeps the values apart.

## SegmentKind

```csharp
public enum SegmentKind
```

Whether a run of a description is fixed words or a number the rules worked out. It is the distinction a UI needs to colour one and not the other.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Text = 0` | Words, punctuation and anything else that never changes. |
| `Value = 1` | A number (or a stand-in such as `X`) that comes from the rules. |

---

## ValueTrend

```csharp
public enum ValueTrend
```

How the modifier pipeline moved a value, from the point of view of whoever uses the entity.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Unchanged = 0` | No modifier touched this value, so the printed number is the real one. |
| `Buffed = 1` | Better than printed: more damage, or a lower cost. |
| `Debuffed = 2` | Worse than printed: less damage, or a higher cost. |
